cohort: The study included 6294 mothers (3247 cases of LBW and 3247 controls with normal birth weight) who had term births and visited healthcare centers in Mashhad, Iran.
finding: Household food insecurity was significantly associated with higher odds of low birth weight (AOR=1.25, 95% CI: 1.03, 1.53).
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was identified as a risk factor, significantly associated with higher odds of LBW (AOR=1.70, 95% CI: 1.40, 2.06).
cross-section timing: Data was collected for term births between March 2019 and March 2022.
birth_weight: Cases had neonates weighing <2500 g, and controls had babies weighing >=2500 g.
